chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from someone else, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadda', who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Among the most blissful of My friends in My presence is a man of light state, possessing a share from prayer, who perfected the worship of his Lord in secrecy, and was hidden among the people. His livelihood was made sufficient (subsistence level), so he was patient with it. His death was hastened, so his inheritance was few and his mourners were few.'

key_terms.خَفِيفَ الْحَالِ: light of state (modest in wealth and status)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of a servant who worships Allah in secret and is patient with modest wealth?
ai.summary: This hadith qudsi, recorded in al-Kafi, highlights the virtue of 'khifaf al-hal' (lightness of condition), where a servant’s modest sustenance and secret worship earn Allah’s delight. The hastening of death serves to preserve the righteous from the trials of prolonged worldly life, resulting in minimal inheritance and mourners as a sign of their detachment from material accumulation.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from someone else, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Abu Ubeyda Al Haza’a who said,

‘I heard Abu Ja’farasws saying: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Allah Mighty and Majestic Said: “The most blissful in Myazwj Presence is a man of light state, with a share from Salāt of good worship of his Lordazwj in the secrecy, and he would be hidden among the people, making his livelihood to be at subsistence level. So he is patient upon it, his death being hastened, and few are his inheritors and few are his mourners’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from more than one person from ‘Asim from ibn Hamid from abu ‘Ubaydah al-Hadhdha’ who has said the following:

“I heard abu Ja’far (a.s.) say, ‘The Messenger of Allah has said, “Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, says, ‘The most envied person among My servants is a man whose needs are light, has a good share in prayer, who performs the worship of his Lord unseen, is obscure among the people, whose expenses are within the limits of bare necessities with which he exercises patience, whose death is quick (like a dead person free from worldly desires) and whose heirs and mourners are very few.’”
